issues.t: Front ball joints and control arms wear out early
issues.sym: Clunking or knocking from the front over bumps, a loose or wobbly feel, and uneven front tire wear, often from about 40,000–50,000 miles.
issues.why: The front lower ball joints and control arm bushings wear quickly. The ball joint and bushings are part of the control arm, so the whole arm usually has to be replaced.
issues.next: Have the front end checked at the first clunk. A badly worn ball joint can separate, so do not wait. Get an alignment after the repair.

issues.t: Tie rod ends wear out early
issues.sym: Clunking or play in the steering, a wandering feel on the highway, and uneven tire wear.
issues.why: The outer tie rod ends wear out early on these cars, often along with the ball joints.
issues.next: Have the steering linkage checked and replace worn tie rod ends, then get an alignment.

issues.sym: Thumping when turning, a sway bar hanging down or rubbing a tire, and visible rot or holes in the frame piece under the engine. In bad cases a control arm mount breaks.
issues.why: The front subframe that holds the engine and front suspension rusts badly in road-salt states.
issues.next: Have the subframe inspected on a lift, especially in snowy states. If it is rotted through, replace it before a suspension mount fails.

issues.sym: A loud whine, grinding or scratching sound from the transmission, often at low speeds, then slipping, loss of drive or a car that will not move.
issues.why: The continuously variable automatic transmission (CVT) used in the Caliber wears internally and can fail, sometimes at low mileage.
issues.next: Check the fluid and have the transmission scanned. CVT fluid must be the correct type. If it is noisy or slipping, get a diagnosis before it leaves you stranded.

issues.sym: The transmission temperature light comes on after 15–25 minutes of highway driving, and the car loses power until it cools down.
issues.why: The CVT runs hot under steady load, and an old or worn unit overheats and protects itself by cutting power.
issues.next: Pull over safely and let it cool. Have the fluid level and condition checked; some owners added an extra cooler, but a failing CVT may need replacing.

issues.sym: Headlights, turn signals or brake lights stop working, the engine stalls, or the car will not crank. The starter may run on its own.
issues.why: The Totally Integrated Power Module, the under-hood fuse and relay box, develops internal faults or corroded relays.
issues.next: Have a shop test the TIPM before replacing the starter or battery. A rebuilt module is cheaper than a new dealer part.

issues.sym: The engine cuts out while driving or at a stop, sometimes with dash lights dimming, and power steering and brake assist get heavy.
issues.why: Owners trace it to a faulty electronic throttle body, corroded connections in the power module, or a weak battery or charging cable. Dealers often could not reproduce it.
issues.next: Get the codes read right after a stall. Have the throttle body, battery cables and power module checked.

issues.t: No start from anti-theft key module
issues.sym: The engine will not crank or start even though the battery is good, sometimes with the security light on.
issues.why: The wireless control module that reads the key and runs the anti-theft system fails, so it will not allow the engine to start. RepairPal lists this as the most common Caliber problem.
issues.next: Have a shop or dealer scan the anti-theft system. A new module usually has to be programmed to your keys.

issues.sym: Wet headliner, wet carpet or water dripping near the front pillars after rain or a car wash.
issues.why: The sunroof drain tubes clog or come loose, so water overflows into the cabin.
issues.next: Have the drain tubes cleared and checked, and dry the carpet to avoid mold and electrical problems.

issues.sym: A loud whine or grinding from the engine bay, the battery light coming on, or the car dying and needing a jump.
issues.why: The alternator bearings or its decoupler pulley wear out. The pulley is often not sold alone, so the alternator is replaced.
issues.next: Have the charging system tested. Replace the alternator before it leaves you stranded.

issues.sym: The car moves after being put in Park and switched off.
issues.why: Owners report a faulty gear shifter or shift cable that did not lock the transmission in Park.
issues.next: Always set the parking brake. If the car moves in Park, have the shifter and cable inspected right away.

issues.t: Airbags and seat belt pretensioners may not work (recall)
issues.sym: Often no warning. The airbag light may come on.
issues.why: The airbag control module can be disabled, so the front and side airbags and seat belt pretensioners may not deploy in a crash. Recall 16V-668.
issues.next: Check your VIN and have the recall done. If the airbag light is on, get it checked soon.

issues.sym: The gas pedal is slow to return or sticks down.
issues.why: The accelerator pedal assembly can bind. Recall 10V-234 addresses it.
issues.next: If the pedal sticks, shift to neutral and brake firmly. Check your VIN for the recall.

issues.sym: ABS or brake warning lights, or unusual braking behavior.
issues.why: A fault in the anti-lock brake control module could cause a loss of control. Recall 06V-493.
issues.next: Check your VIN and have the free fix done.

issues.t: Rear wheel hub bolts may loosen (recall)
issues.sym: Clicking or looseness from a rear wheel, or the parking brake not holding well.
issues.why: Rear wheel hub mounting bolts on some early cars may not be tightened correctly. Recall 07V-196.
issues.next: Check your VIN and have the hubs inspected for free.

issues.t: Engine computer or fuel pump relay can cause stalling (recall)
issues.why: A problem with the powertrain control module or fuel pump relay can shut the engine off. Recall 08V-528.
issues.next: Check your VIN and have the recall done.
